title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Summary of the National Court Intellectual Property Trial Work Conference on Several Issues concerning the Adjudication of Technology Contract Disputes
keywords_en: contract dispute; intellectual property; conference regarding trial of technology contract disputes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular on Issuing the Summary of the National Court Intellectual Property Adjudication Work Conference on Certain Issues Concerning the Trial of Technology Contract Disputes

Fa [2001] No. 84

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Summary of the National Court Intellectual Property Adjudication Work Conference on Certain Issues Concerning the Trial of Technology Contract Disputes is hereby issued for your earnest implementation.

June 19, 2001

National Court Intellectual Property Adjudication Work Conference

Summary of Certain Issues Concerning the Trial of Technology Contract Disputes

(June 15, 2001)

On March 15, 1999, the Second Session of the Ninth National People's Congress adopted the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), which came into effect on October 1 of the same year. The promulgation and implementation of the Contract Law ended the coexistence of three separate contract laws—the Economic Contract Law, the Foreign-Related Economic Contract Law, and the Technology Contract Law—and achieved the unification of these three contract laws. Significant changes have occurred in China's contract legal system. According to the Contract Law, the Technology Contract Law was abolished, and its main contents have been absorbed into Chapter 18 of the Specific Provisions of the Contract Law, titled "Technology Contracts." Correspondingly, the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court, the "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the Trial of Science and Technology Dispute Cases," formulated based on the Technology Contract Law and its Implementing Regulations, was also abolished. To adapt to the major changes in China's contract legal system and achieve a smooth transition between the old and new contract legal systems, the Supreme People's Court is planning and gradually formulating judicial interpretations on the Contract Law. It has already issued the "Interpretation (I) on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," and the judicial interpretation on the technology contract part is listed as "Interpretation (III) on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China."

In August 1999, the Supreme People's Court began drafting "Interpretation (III)." Based on a review of the original technology contract laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations, and in light of the new provisions of the Contract Law on technology contracts and new situations and issues arising in trial practice, a draft for comments was formed. In November 1999, to implement the Contract Law, the Supreme People's Court held a national forum on technology contract adjudication work in Hefei City, Anhui Province. Nearly 70 representatives from 31 high people's courts, 22 intermediate people's courts, and 2 basic people's courts attended the meeting. Vice President Li Guoguang attended the meeting and delivered an important speech. The draft for comments was fully discussed at the forum, and nearly 20 courts submitted written opinions. Representatives from the Ministry of Science and Technology and the State Intellectual Property Office also attended the meeting. In early April 2000, the former Intellectual Property Division and the Ministry of Science and Technology jointly held a seminar on legal issues of technology contracts in Xi'an City, again soliciting opinions on the draft for comments from some local science and technology commissions, science and technology associations, intellectual property litigation lawyers, and patent agents. Thereafter, written opinions were solicited from 8 departments, including the Legislative Affairs Commission of the National People's Congress Standing Committee and the Legislative Affairs Office of the State Council, and from 11 experts, including Zheng Chengsi and Liang Huixing. After extensive solicitation of opinions and repeated revisions, a review draft was formed.

From June 12 to 15, 2001, the Supreme People's Court held a national conference on intellectual property adjudication work in Shanghai. Over 120 participants attended, including: vice presidents in charge of intellectual property adjudication work from 30 high people's courts, the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Xinjiang High People's Court, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and 24 intermediate people's courts; directors or deputy directors of intellectual property divisions or business divisions responsible for intellectual property adjudication; responsible comrades from the Legislative Affairs Commission of the National People's Congress Standing Committee, the Education, Science, Culture and Health Committee of the National People's Congress, the Legislative Affairs Office of the State Council, the Ministry of Science and Technology, the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, the State Intellectual Property Office, and the National Copyright Administration; and renowned experts and scholars from the Intellectual Property Center of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the Law School of Tsinghua University, the Intellectual Property School of Peking University, and the Intellectual Property Teaching and Research Center of Renmin University of China. Vice President Cao Jianming of the Supreme People's Court attended the meeting and delivered a speech. The conference analyzed the current situation facing intellectual property adjudication work, summarized the experience of nearly two decades of intellectual property adjudication, and deployed the tasks for intellectual property adjudication by people's courts in the current and future period. The conference focused on in-depth discussions on topics such as the impact of China's accession to the WTO on intellectual property adjudication work and the preparations required, the implementation of the newly revised Patent Law, Contract Law, and other intellectual property laws, and the full utilization of the overall function of intellectual property adjudication. The conference also discussed several issues concerning the application of law in technology contract dispute cases. The conference believed that, to meet the urgent needs of people's courts in trying technology contract dispute cases at present, it is necessary to issue to all people's courts a summary of principles that have matured regarding the application of law in trying technology contract disputes, as guidance for the nationwide trial of technology contract dispute cases. In implementation, courts at all levels should continue to accumulate experience and promptly report issues arising during implementation to the Third Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court, so as to further improve the draft judicial interpretation on the application of law in technology contract disputes, and formally issue and implement it after the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court discusses and approves it. The following summary is now provided on certain issues concerning the application of law in trying technology contract dispute cases:

I. General Provisions

(1) Technology Achievements and Technology Secrets

1. The term "technology achievements" as used in Chapter 18 of the Contract Law refers to technical solutions, including products, processes, materials, and improvements thereof, made using scientific and technical knowledge, information, and experience, and includes patents, patent applications, technology secrets, and other technology achievements that can obtain intellectual property rights (such as new plant varieties, computer software, integrated circuit layout designs, and new drug achievements).

2. The term "technology secrets" as used in Chapter 18 of the Contract Law refers to technical information that is not known to the public, can bring economic benefits to the right holder, is practical, and has been subject to confidentiality measures taken by the right holder.

The term "not known to the public" in the preceding paragraph means that the overall or precise combination or elements of the technical information are not generally known or readily accessible to persons within the circles that normally deal with the information concerned. "Can bring economic benefits to the right holder, is practical" means that the technical information has commercial value due to being a secret, enabling its owner to obtain economic benefits or gain a competitive advantage. "The right holder has taken confidentiality measures" means that the lawful owner of the technical information has taken reasonable measures under the circumstances such that, under normal conditions, the technical information can be kept confidential.

The term "technology secrets" in the Contract Law is synonymous with "technology secret achievements."

(2) Service Technology Achievements and Non-Service Technology Achievements

3. If a legal person or other organization and its employee have agreed in a labor contract or other agreement on the rights and interests of technology achievements completed by the employee during employment or after resignation, the agreement shall be followed for confirmation. This does not apply if the agreement shall be deemed invalid or shall be revoked or terminated according to law.

4. The term "carrying out the tasks of the legal person or other organization" as used in the second paragraph of Article 326 of the Contract Law means:

(1) The employee performs the duties of his or her post or undertakes other scientific research and technology development tasks assigned by the legal person or other organization.

(2) Within one year after resignation, termination, or retirement, the employee continues to engage in scientific research and technology development related to the post duties or assigned tasks of the original legal person or other organization, unless otherwise provided by law or administrative regulations, or otherwise agreed by the parties.

The term "post duties" in the preceding paragraph refers to the tasks and scope of responsibilities of the employee's position as stipulated by the legal person or other organization.

5. The term "material and technical conditions" in the second paragraph of Article 326 of the Contract Law refers to funds, equipment, materials, raw materials, and undisclosed technical information and data.

The term "mainly utilizing the material and technical conditions of the legal person or other organization" in the second paragraph of Article 326 of the Contract Law means that, during the research and development process of completing the technology achievement, the employee uses all or most of the funds, equipment, materials, or raw materials of the legal person or other organization, or the substantive content of the technology achievement is completed based on the undisclosed technology achievements, interim technology achievements, or key technologies of the legal person or other organization. This does not apply if the parties have agreed to repay the funds or pay a usage fee for the use of the material and technical conditions provided by the legal person or other organization.

Using technical information that has been disclosed by the legal person or other organization to the public or is already known to persons of ordinary skill in the art during the research and development process, or using the material conditions of the legal person or other organization to verify or test the technical solution after the completion of the technology achievement, does not constitute "mainly utilizing the material and technical conditions of the legal person or other organization."

6. Where the technology achievement is completed by an individual who has both carried out the tasks of the original legal person or other organization and mainly utilized the material and technical conditions of the current legal person or other organization for the same scientific research or technology development project, the rights and interests of the technology achievement shall be determined by agreement between the original legal person or other organization and the current legal person or other organization. If no agreement can be reached, the two parties shall reasonably share the rights and interests.

7. The rights and interests of technology achievements completed by an employee in part-time work outside his or her post duties or the tasks assigned by the legal person or other organization, or through cooperation with others, shall be determined according to the agreement with the employing party (part-time unit) or collaborator. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and a supplementary agreement cannot be reached in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the determination shall be made in accordance with Articles 326 and 327 of the Contract Law.

When handling in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the technical rights and interests of the legal person or other organization where the employee works shall not be prejudiced.

8. The term "individual who has completed a technology achievement" in Articles 326 and 327 of the Contract Law refers to a person who has made creative contributions, individually or jointly, to the technology achievement. It does not include persons who only provided funds, equipment, materials, or test conditions; persons engaged in organizational management; or persons who provided auxiliary services such as assisting in drawing diagrams, organizing materials, or translating documents.

In judging creative contributions, the substantive technical components of the technology achievement shall be analyzed. The person who proposes the substantive technical components and the technical solution realized thereby is the person who made the creative contribution. The person who made creative contributions to the technology achievement is the inventor or designer.

(3) Subject of Technology Contracts

9. If a scientific research organization established by a legal person or other organization for engaging in technology research, development, or transfer activities (including project teams, work studios, etc.), which does not have civil subject status, enters into a technology contract, and such legal person or other organization authorized or ratified the contract, the contract shall be deemed as concluded by such legal person or other organization, and such legal person or other organization shall bear liability. If the contract was not authorized or ratified by such legal person or other organization, the members of the scientific research organization shall bear joint liability. However, if such legal person or other organization benefited from the contract, it shall bear corresponding liability within the scope of such benefit.

(4) Validity of Technology Contracts

10. A technology contract shall not be invalid due to any of the following reasons:

(1) The technology that is the subject matter of the contract has not undergone technical appraisal;

(2) The technology contract has not been registered or filed with the relevant authorities;

(3) A patent implementation license contract is concluded with respect to a technology for which a patent application has been filed but no patent right has been granted yet.

11. If a technology contract contains any of the following circumstances, it falls under the circumstance of "unlawfully monopolizing technology and impeding technological progress" as referred to in Article 329 of the Contract Law:

(1) Restricting the other party from conducting new research and development on the basis of the subject matter technology of the contract, or imposing unequal conditions for the exchange of improved technologies, including requiring one party to provide its own improved technology to the other party free of charge, transfer it to the other party on a non-reciprocal basis, or free of charge exclusively or share the intellectual property rights of such improved technology;

(2) Restricting the other party from acquiring technology from other sources;

(3) Obstructing the other party from fully implementing the subject matter technology of the contract in a reasonable manner according to market demand, including unreasonably restricting the quantity, variety, price, sales channels, and export markets of products produced or services provided by the technology recipient using the subject matter technology of the contract;

(4) Requiring the technology recipient to accept incidental conditions that are not essential for implementing the technology, including purchasing technology, services, raw materials, equipment, or products that the technology recipient does not need, and accepting personnel that the technology recipient does not need;

(5) Unreasonably restricting the technology recipient's freedom to choose raw materials, components, or equipment from different sources;

(6) Prohibiting the technology recipient from challenging the validity of the intellectual property rights of the subject matter technology of the contract.

12. If a technology contract contains any of the following circumstances, it falls under the circumstance of "infringing upon another person's technology achievements" as referred to in Article 329 of the Contract Law:

(1) Infringing upon another person's patent rights, patent application rights, or patent implementation rights;

(2) Infringing upon another person's rights to use or transfer technology secret achievements;

(3) Infringing upon another person's new plant variety rights, new plant variety application rights, or new plant variety implementation rights;

(4) Infringing upon another person's computer software copyright, integrated circuit layout design rights, new drug achievement rights, or other technology achievement rights;

(5) Infringing upon another person's invention rights, discovery rights, or other scientific and technological achievement rights.

If a contract infringes upon the personal rights of the person who completed the technology achievement, such as invention rights, discovery rights, or other scientific and technological achievement rights, the part of the contract involving the infringement shall be invalid. If the invalidity of that part does not affect the validity of other parts, the other parts shall remain valid.

13. If a party uses or transfers a technology secret that it has independently developed or otherwise lawfully obtained, which is identical or similar to another person's technology secret, such act does not constitute "infringing upon another person's technology achievements" as referred to in Article 329 of the Contract Law.

Grasping relevant technology through lawful means such as visits and inspections, or through reverse engineering means such as disassembly, surveying, and mapping, and analysis of lawfully obtained products, falls under the circumstance of "otherwise lawfully obtained" as referred to in the preceding paragraph, unless otherwise provided by law or agreed by the parties.

14. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties or ratified by the right holder of the technology achievement, a contract concluded by the transferee under a technology secret transfer contract or a patent implementation license contract for transferring the subject matter technology of such contract to a third party shall be invalid.

15. If a technology transfer contract contains both the content of patent right transfer or patent implementation license and the content of technology secret transfer, and the patent right is declared invalid or the technology secret is disclosed by others, the validity of the other part of the contract shall not be affected, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

16. If one party, by fraudulent means, uses its existing technology achievement as the subject matter of research and development to enter into an entrusted development contract with another party and collects research and development fees, or, for the same research and development project, enters into separate entrusted development contracts with two or more principals successively and collects research and development fees repeatedly, the injured party may request modification or rescission of the contract in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 54 of the Contract Law. However, if the circumstances fall under Article 52 or Article 329 of the Contract Law and the contract should be dealt with as invalid, that shall prevail.

17. After a technology contract is invalidated or rescinded, if the research developer, transferor, or受托人 (trustee) has performed the agreed obligations, and the fault causing the invalidity or rescission lies with the other party, the research and development funds, technology use fees, and remuneration for providing consulting services that such party should have collected according to the agreement may be deemed as losses suffered by such party due to the invalidity or rescission of the contract caused by the other party's reasons.

18. After a technology contract is invalidated or rescinded, the parties shall return to the right holder technical carriers such as technical documents, samples, and prototypes obtained under the contract, and shall not retain reproductions thereof. If a technology secret is involved, the parties are legally obligated to maintain confidentiality.

19. After a technology contract is invalidated or rescinded, the ownership and benefit sharing of new technology achievements completed through the performance of the contract, or of subsequent improvement parts completed on the basis of another person's technology achievements, if the parties cannot reach a new agreement, shall be enjoyed by the party who completed the technology achievement.

20. After a technology contract that infringes upon another person's rights to use or transfer technology secret achievements is invalidated, unless otherwise provided by law or administrative regulations, a party who has obtained the technology secret in good faith and for value may continue to use the technology secret, provided that it pays reasonable usage fees to the right holder and undertakes confidentiality obligations. Unless an agreement is reached with the right holder, the party obtaining the technology secret in good faith (user) shall not exceed the scope of use determined at the time of obtaining the technology secret when continuing to use it. If the parties maliciously collude, or one party knows or should have known that the other party is infringing and still enters into or performs the contract with it, such conduct constitutes joint infringement, and the parties shall bear joint and several liability for compensation and confidentiality obligations. The party that obtained the technology secret under such invalid contract shall not continue to use the technology secret.

The usage fee as referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be determined by agreement between the user and the right holder. If no agreement can be reached, either party may request a people's court to make a ruling. If the user refuses to perform the usage fee agreement reached by both parties, the right holder may, in addition to requesting the people's court to order the user to pay the usage fee for the period during which the user has used the technology secret, also request the people's court to order the user to cease using the technology secret. If the user refuses to comply with the people's court's ruling on the usage fee, the right holder may, in addition to applying for compulsory enforcement of the usage fee for the period already used, also request the people's court to order the user to cease using the technology secret. Before the parties reach an agreement on the usage fee or the people's court makes an effective ruling, the user may not be required to cease using the technology secret.

21. When a people's court determines the usage fee under the preceding article, it may determine the amount based on the fee that the right holder would have charged for a good-faith transfer of the technology secret to a third party, taking into account factors such as the user's scale of use and economic benefits. Alternatively, it may determine the amount based on the fee paid by the user to obtain the technology secret, taking into account factors such as the research and development cost of the technology secret, the degree of transformation and application of the achievement, and the user's scale of use and economic benefits.

The people's court shall simultaneously rule on the usage fee for the period already used and the payment standard for future use.

After the contract is confirmed invalid, the user shall pay to the right holder the usage fee for the period during which the user has used the technology secret, regardless of whether the user continues to use the technology secret. The fees paid by the user to the transferor of the invalid contract shall be returned by the transferor. The portion of such fees that the transferor has directly paid to the right holder as compensation for infringement damages shall be correspondingly deducted when calculating the usage fee to be paid by the user to the right holder.

22. If laws or regulations require that approval formalities or licenses be obtained from relevant authorities for the production of products or the provision of services, but such approval formalities have not been completed or such licenses have not been obtained, this does not affect the validity of the technology contract concluded by the parties concerning the production of such products or the provision of such services.

If the parties have no agreement or the agreement is unclear on the obligation to undergo the approval formalities or obtain the license referred to in the preceding paragraph, and a supplementary agreement cannot be reached in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the party implementing the technology shall be responsible for undergoing such formalities or obtaining such license, unless otherwise provided by laws or regulations.

5. Determination of the Subject Matter of a Technology Contract

23. Where the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the price, remuneration, or royalty of a technology contract, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the people's court may handle the matter according to the following principles:

(1) For technology development contracts and technology transfer contracts, a reasonable determination shall be made based on factors such as the research and development costs of the relevant technological achievements, their advancement, the degree of implementation, transformation, and application, the rights and interests enjoyed and responsibilities borne by the parties, and the economic and social benefits of the technological achievements;

(2) For technology consulting contracts and technology service contracts, a reasonable determination shall be made based on factors such as the quantity, quality, and technological content of the consulting or service work, as well as the expected economic and social benefits.

Where the price, remuneration, or royalty includes non-technical components, these shall be calculated separately.

24. Where the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the place of performance of a technology contract, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, for a technology development contract, the place of performance shall be the location of the research developer; however, for a contract concluded under Article 330, paragraph 4 of the Contract Law, the place of performance shall be the place where the technological achievements are implemented. For a technology transfer contract, the place of performance shall be the location of the transferee; for a technology consulting contract, the place of performance shall be the location of the trustee; for a technology service contract, the place of performance shall be the location of the client. However, for payment of the contract price, remuneration, or royalty, the place of performance shall be the location of the party receiving such payment.

25. Where the parties to a technology contract have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the acceptance standards for technological achievements, and when applying the provisions of Article 62 of the Contract Law, if there are no national standards, industry standards, or professional technical standards, the contract shall be performed in accordance with the general technical requirements that are practical for the industry.

The forecasts and analyses of economic benefits or cost indicators in the feasibility analysis report made by the parties when concluding the technology contract shall not be deemed as the acceptance standards agreed in the contract, unless the parties have otherwise agreed.

6. Termination of Technology Contracts and Liability for Breach of Contract

26. Where one party to a technology contract delays in performing its principal obligation, and after a demand for performance, fails to perform within 30 days, the other party may terminate the contract in accordance with Article 94, subparagraph (3) of the Contract Law.

If the demand notice includes a performance period that exceeds 30 days, termination may only occur upon expiration of that period.

27. Under any of the following circumstances, where performance of the technology contract becomes unnecessary or impossible, a party may terminate the contract in accordance with Article 94, subparagraph (4) of the Contract Law:

(1) Due to a party's breach of contract, the material conditions necessary for contract performance are lost or severely damaged, and cannot be replaced or repaired;

(2) The project or technology that is the subject of the technology contract, due to violation of scientific principles or existence of major defects, cannot achieve the agreed technical and economic benefit indicators;

28. In a patent exploitation license contract or a technical secret transfer contract where the royalty is to be paid on a royalty basis, if the transferee, without justifiable reason, fails to exploit the subject technology of the contract and thereby refuses to pay the royalty, the transferor may terminate the contract in accordance with Article 94, subparagraph (4) of the Contract Law.

29. During the term of a technical secret transfer contract, if the subject technology of the contract is disclosed and has entered the public domain due to reasons not attributable to the transferee, the parties may terminate the contract, unless otherwise agreed.

30. During the performance of a technology contract, if one party commits a technical error that can be promptly corrected, or makes necessary technical adjustments to adapt to changes in circumstances, and such error or adjustment does not affect the realization of the contract purpose, it shall not be considered a breach of contract. The additional expenses incurred thereby shall be borne by the party itself. However, if the party fails to fulfill its obligation to give notice in accordance with Article 60, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, thereby causing losses to the other party, the party shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract.

31. In performing a technology contract, if the technical medium and content delivered for the provision of technological achievements or consulting services are inconsistent with the agreement, the delivering party shall promptly correct or supplement them. If the correction or supplementation is not made in a timely manner, or if the correction or supplementation causes losses or additional burdens to the other party, the party shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract. This shall not apply if the technical improvements made by one party render the contract performance more positive or advantageous than originally agreed.

7. Characterization of Technology Contracts

32. Where parties combine the contents of a technology contract with those of other contracts into a single contract, or combine the contents of different types of technology contracts into one contract, the nature of the case and the cause of action shall be determined based on the rights and obligations in dispute among the parties, and the corresponding laws and regulations shall apply.

33. If the name of a technology contract is inconsistent with the rights and obligations agreed in the contract, the type of contract and the cause of action shall be determined in accordance with the rights and obligations agreed in the contract, and the corresponding laws and regulations shall apply.

34. A contract entered into by the parties with technology development, transfer, consulting, or service as the contract content shall be considered a technology contract.

35. For a contract that transfers staged technological achievements and stipulates obligations for subsequent development, if a dispute arises regarding the repeat test effects of the staged technological achievements, it shall be handled as a technology transfer contract; if a dispute arises regarding the subsequent development, it shall be handled as a technology development contract.

36. Where a technology transfer contract stipulates that the transferor shall provide the transferee with special equipment or raw materials for implementing the technology, or provide related technical consulting or technical services, such stipulations shall be part of the technology transfer contract. If a dispute arises from such stipulations, it shall be handled as a technology transfer contract.

37. Where parties conclude a joint venture contract in the form of technology contribution, but the technology contributor does not participate in the management and operation of the joint venture, and stipulates in the form of a guaranteed return clause that the joint venture or the other joint venture party shall pay a price or royalty for the technology, such contract shall be considered a technology transfer contract.

38. Where a technology transfer contract includes a stipulation that the transferor is responsible for exclusive distribution (repurchase) of the products manufactured by the transferee using the subject technology, and a dispute arises solely from the transferor's failure or incomplete performance of the exclusive distribution (repurchase) obligation without involving technical issues, the cause of action shall be determined according to the rights and obligations stipulated in the exclusive distribution (repurchase) clause, and the corresponding legal provisions shall apply.

39. A contract where one party to a technology development contract only provides material conditions such as funds, equipment, and materials, and undertakes auxiliary cooperation matters, while the other party conducts the research and development work, shall be considered a commissioned development contract.

40. Where one party, in the name of technology transfer, provides technology that has already entered the public domain, and provides technical guidance, imparts technical knowledge, etc., to solve specific technical problems for the other party, the contract thus concluded may be deemed to be performed as a technology service contract, unless the circumstances fall under the provisions of Articles 52 and 54 of the Contract Law.

8. Application of Law to Technology Contracts with Several Special Subjects

41. For contract disputes concerning the transfer of new drug technologies, transfer of plant variety application rights, transfer and licensing of plant variety rights, the general provisions of the Contract Law shall apply, and reference may be made to the provisions of Chapter 18 of the Contract Law and this Summary regarding technology transfer contracts, unless otherwise provided by law.

42. For contract disputes concerning the development, license, or transfer of computer software, if the Copyright Law or other laws have special provisions, those provisions shall apply; if there are no such provisions, the general provisions of the Contract Law shall apply, and reference may be made to the provisions of Chapter 18 of the Contract Law and relevant provisions of this Summary.

II. Technology Development Contracts

(A) Related Concepts

43. The term "new technology, new product, new process, new material and its system" as referred to in Article 330 of the Contract Law means a technical solution such as a product, process, material, or system that the parties have not yet mastered at the time of concluding the technology contract. However, this does not include modifications of existing products, changes in processes, adjustments in material formulations, or verification, testing, and use of technological achievements that do not involve technical innovation.

44. The contract between parties for the transformation and implementation of scientific and technological achievements with industrial application value, as referred to in Article 330, paragraph 4 of the Contract Law, means a contract between parties regarding scientific and technological achievements (including staged achievements) that have practical value but have not yet been commercialized or industrially applied, with the purpose of achieving commercialization and industrial application of such achievements, and stipulating matters concerning subsequent testing, development, and application.

45. The term "participating in research and development work with a division of labor" as referred to in Article 335 of the Contract Law means jointly or separately undertaking tasks such as design, process, testing, and trial production in accordance with the agreed plan and division of work.

46. The right to use and the right to transfer technical secret achievements as referred to in Article 341 of the Contract Law mean the rights acquired by the parties under legal provisions or contractual agreements to use or transfer the technical secret achievements. The right to use means the right to use the technical secret achievements oneself or to license others to use them for production or business purposes; the right to transfer means the right to assign the technical secret achievements to others.

47. The term "each party has the right to use and transfer" as referred to in Article 341 of the Contract Law means that each party has the right, without the consent of the other party, to itself use the technical secret or to license others to use it by way of a non-exclusive license, and to exclusively retain the benefits derived therefrom. If one party intends to assign all of its rights to use and transfer the technical secret achievements to others, or to license others to use the technical secret by way of an exclusive or sole license, it must obtain the consent of the other party.

(B) Rights and Obligations of the Parties

48. The commissioning party in a commissioned development contract has the right, under Article 60, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, without hindering the normal work of the research developer, to carry out necessary supervision and inspection of the research developer's contract performance and use of research and development funds, including inspecting accounts and visiting the site.

The research developer has the right, under Article 331 of the Contract Law, to request the commissioning party to supplement necessary background materials and data, etc., but not beyond the scope necessary for contract performance.

49. Upon acceptance of research and development achievements, the commissioning party in a commissioned development contract and the parties in a cooperative development contract have the right to obtain the technical materials, test reports, and data necessary for implementing the technological achievements, and to request the other party to provide necessary technical guidance to ensure that the provided technological achievements meet the conditions agreed in the contract.

50. In accordance with Article 339, paragraph 1 and Article 340, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law, where the patent right obtained from technological achievements developed under a commissioned or cooperative development contract is jointly owned by the parties, the method of exploiting the patent and the allocation of benefits shall be agreed upon by the parties. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, and no supplementary agreement can be reached under Article 61 of the Contract Law, each party has the right to exploit the patent itself, and the benefits derived therefrom shall belong to the exploiting party.

If a party does not have the conditions to independently exploit the patent, it may be regarded as exploiting the patent itself if it licenses one legal person or other organization to exploit the patent by way of a non-exclusive license, or cooperates with one legal person, other organization, or natural person to exploit the patent, or exploits the patent through technology contribution in a joint venture.

51. In accordance with Article 341 of the Contract Law, where one party only has the right to itself use the technical secret, but lacks the conditions to independently use it, it may be regarded as itself using the technical secret if it licenses one legal person or other organization to use the technical secret by way of a non-exclusive license, or cooperates with one legal person, other organization, or natural person to use the technical secret, or uses the technical secret through technology contribution in a joint venture.

III. Technology Transfer Contracts

(A) General Provisions on Technology Transfer Contracts

52. The term "technology transfer contract" as referred to in Article 342 of the Contract Law means a contract entered into by the legal owner of the technology, including a person authorized to transfer the technology externally, to assign to another or license another to use the relevant rights in a specific and existing patent, patent application, or technical secret. It does not include contracts concluded regarding technological achievements that are yet to be researched and developed, or regarding knowledge, technology, experience, or information that does not involve patents, patent applications, or technical secrets. Among them:

(1) A patent right assignment contract means a contract entered into by the patentee to assign its patent right to the assignee, and the assignee pays a price.

(2) A patent application right assignment contract means a contract entered into by the transferor to assign to the transferee the right to apply for a patent for its specific technological achievement, and the transferee pays a price.

(3) A technical secret transfer contract means a contract entered into by the holder of the technical secret achievement or its authorized person, as the transferor, to provide the technical secret to the transferee, clarify the rights to use and transfer the technical secret achievement between them, and the transferee pays a price or royalty.

(4) A patent exploitation license contract means a contract entered into by the patentee or its authorized person, as the licensor, to license the licensee to exploit the patent within the agreed scope, and the licensee pays a royalty.

53. In a technology transfer contract, the transferor shall guarantee that the transferee can achieve the agreed technical indicators when exploiting the technology in the agreed manner. Unless it is explicitly agreed that the transferor guarantees that the transferee will achieve the agreed economic benefit indicators, the transferor shall not be liable for the economic benefits after the transferee exploits the technology.

When transferring staged technological achievements, the transferor shall guarantee that repeated tests under certain conditions can achieve the expected results.

54. Where a technology transfer contract stipulates that the technology acquired by the transferee must undergo small-scale testing, pilot-scale testing, and industrial testing before being put into batch production, the transferor shall not bear liability for losses incurred by the transferee if it directly puts the technology into batch production without such testing.

55. The term "scope of exploiting the patent or using the technical secret" as referred to in Article 343 of the Contract Law means the term, territory, and manner of exploiting the patent or using the technical secret, as well as the personnel having access to the technical secret, etc.

56. The term "subsequent improvement" as referred to in Article 354 of the Contract Law means an innovation or improvement made by one or more parties to the subject technology of the contract during the term of the technology transfer contract.

57. For a license contract concluded between parties regarding a technological achievement for which a patent application has been filed, before the patent application is published, the relevant provisions of technical secret transfer contracts shall apply; after the invention patent application is published but before it is granted, the relevant provisions of patent exploitation license contracts shall be referred to; after the patent is granted, the original contract shall become a patent exploitation license contract, and the relevant provisions of patent exploitation license contracts shall apply.

(B) Patent Right Assignment Contracts and Patent Application Right Assignment Contracts

58. If, before concluding a patent right assignment contract or a patent application right assignment contract, the transferor has already exploited the invention-creation itself, unless otherwise agreed by the parties, after the contract takes effect, the transferee has the right to require the transferor to cease exploitation.

After the patent right or patent application right is assigned to the transferee in accordance with the Patent Law, the transferee may exercise rights against others as the patentee or patent applicant according to law.

59. A patent right assignment contract or a patent application right assignment contract shall not affect the validity of a patent exploitation license contract or a technical secret transfer contract that the transferor concluded with others before the establishment of the assignment contract. The rights and obligations among the relevant parties shall be determined in accordance with Chapter 5 of the Contract Law.

60. If the patent application is rejected before the patent application right is assigned to the transferee in accordance with the Patent Law, the parties may terminate the patent application right assignment contract; if the patent application is rejected after being assigned to the transferee, the validity of the contract shall not be affected, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

If the patent application is rejected because, at the time of the establishment of the patent application right assignment contract, there was a prior patent application for the same invention-creation that had not yet been published, the parties may, in accordance with Article 54, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Contract Law, request to modify or rescind the contract.

(C) Patent Exploitation License Contracts

61. The transferor in a patent exploitation license contract shall maintain the validity of the patent right during the term of the contract, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

During the term of the contract, if the patent right is terminated due to the transferor's fault, the transferee may terminate the contract in accordance with Article 94, subparagraph (4) of the Contract Law, and the transferor shall bear liability for breach of contract; if the patent right is declared invalid, the contract shall cease to be performed, and the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Patent Law.

62. If a patent exploitation license contract does not stipulate or does not clearly stipulate the term for exploiting the patent, and no supplementary agreement can be reached under Article 61 of the Contract Law, the licensee's exploitation of the patent shall not be limited by any term.

63. A patent exploitation license may be an exclusive license, a sole license, or a non-exclusive license.

The term "sole license" in the preceding paragraph means that the transferor has no right to license the same patent to another party within the scope already licensed to the transferee; "exclusive license" means that the transferor has no right to license the same patent to another party or to exploit it itself within the scope already licensed to the transferee; "non-exclusive license" means that the transferor may still license the same patent to another party within the scope already licensed to the transferee.

If the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the type of license, and no supplementary agreement can be reached under Article 61 of the Contract Law, the license shall be deemed a non-exclusive license.

If a patent exploitation license contract stipulates that the transferee may sublicense the patent to others, such sublicense shall be a non-exclusive license, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

64. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the right to exploit a patent obtained under a compulsory license decision shall be a non-exclusive license.

65. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, if the transferor under a sole license contract does not have the conditions to independently exploit its patent, and cooperates with one legal person, other organization, or natural person to exploit the patent, or exploits the patent through technology contribution, this may be regarded as the transferor exploiting the patent itself. However, if the transferor separately cooperates or enters into joint ventures with two or more legal persons, other organizations, or natural persons to exploit the same patent, such conduct shall constitute a breach of contract by unauthorizedly licensing a third party to exploit the patent as provided in Article 351 of the Contract Law.

66. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, if the transferee under a patent exploitation license contract cooperates with others or enters into a joint venture by contributing the licensed patent, such conduct shall constitute unauthorizedly licensing a third party to exploit the patent without the transferor's consent as provided in Article 352 of the Contract Law.

(D) Technical Secret Transfer Contracts

67. If a technical secret transfer contract does not stipulate or does not clearly stipulate the term for using the technical secret, and no supplementary agreement can be reached under Article 61 of the Contract Law, the transferee may use the technical secret indefinitely.

68. The confidentiality obligation of the transferor under a technical secret transfer contract as referred to in Article 347 of the Contract Law shall not affect its right to apply for a patent, unless the parties agree that the transferor shall not apply for a patent or expressly stipulate that the transferor bears a confidentiality obligation.

69. The transfer of a technical secret may adopt the licensing methods provided in paragraph 63 of this Summary, and reference shall be made to the relevant provisions of the Contract Law and this Summary regarding the methods of exploitation licensing of patents.

IV. Technology Consulting Contracts and Technology Service Contracts

(A) Technology Consulting Contracts

70. The specific technical projects referred to in paragraph 1 of Article 356 of the Contract Law of the PRC include soft science research projects concerning the coordinated development of science and technology with economy and society, technical projects aimed at promoting scientific and technological progress and management modernization, improving economic and social benefits, and other professional technical projects.

71. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the expenses incurred by the consultant of a technical consultation contract for conducting investigations, research, analysis, demonstration, tests, measurements, etc., shall be borne by the consultant itself.

72. If the parties have not agreed on an obligation of confidentiality regarding the technical data and materials provided by the client or the consultation reports and opinions proposed by the consultant under a technical consultation contract, each party has the right to cite, publish, and provide to third parties such data, materials, reports, and opinions, provided that the legitimate rights and interests of the other party are not infringed.

73. If the consultant under a technical consultation contract discovers obvious errors or defects in the data, materials, etc., provided by the client, the consultant shall promptly notify the client. The client shall promptly respond and make corrections within the agreed period.

If the consultant fails to promptly notify the client of the problems mentioned in the preceding paragraph, it shall be deemed that the consultant accepts that the technical data, materials, etc., provided by the client meet the agreed conditions.

(2) Technical Service Contracts

74. The specific technical problems referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 356 of the Contract Law of the PRC refer to problems that require the application of scientific and technical knowledge to solve issues in professional technical work related to improving product structure, improving process flow, enhancing product quality, reducing product cost, saving resources and energy, protecting resources and environment, achieving safe operation, and improving economic and social benefits.

75. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the expenses required for the service provider to complete the service items and solve the technical problems under a technical service contract shall be borne by the service provider itself.

76. If the service provider under a technical service contract discovers that the working conditions provided by the client, such as data, materials, samples, materials, and site, do not conform to the agreement, the service provider shall promptly notify the client. The client shall promptly respond and make corrections within the agreed period.

If the service provider fails to promptly notify the client of the problems mentioned in the preceding paragraph, it shall be deemed that the service provider accepts that the working conditions provided by the client meet the agreed conditions.

77. If, during the performance of a technical service contract, the service provider discovers that continuing the work may cause damage to materials, samples, or equipment, it shall suspend the work and promptly notify the client or make recommendations. The client shall respond within the agreed period.

If the service provider does not suspend work or fails to promptly notify the client and take appropriate measures, or if the client fails to respond within the time limit, the responsible party shall bear the corresponding liability for the dangerous consequences arising therefrom.

(3) Technical Training Contracts

78. The technical training contract referred to in Article 364 of the Contract Law of the PRC refers to a contract concluded by one party entrusting the other party to provide professional technical training and guidance to designated personnel (trainees) on specific projects, excluding vocational training, cultural education, and on-the-job education conducted according to industry or unit plans.

79. The main obligations of the client under a technical training contract are to dispatch qualified trainees as agreed; to ensure that trainees abide by training discipline and receive professional technical training and guidance; and to pay remuneration as agreed.

The main obligations of the trainer under a technical training contract are to assign qualified instructors as agreed; to formulate and implement training plans, complete training on schedule; and to achieve the agreed training objectives.

80. If the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the responsibility for providing and managing the necessary venues, facilities, and test conditions for technical training, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the client shall be responsible for providing and managing them.

81. If the trainees dispatched by the client under a technical training contract do not meet the agreed conditions and affect the training quality, the client shall pay remuneration as agreed.

If the instructors assigned by the trainer do not meet the agreed conditions and affect the training quality, or if the trainer fails to conduct training according to the plan and project, resulting in failure to achieve the agreed training objectives, the trainer shall bear liability for breach of contract by reducing or waiving remuneration.

If the trainer discovers that the trainees do not meet the agreed conditions or the client discovers that the instructors do not meet the agreed conditions, the discovering party shall promptly notify the other party to make a replacement. The other party shall make the replacement within the agreed period. If the notification is not made promptly or the replacement is not made as agreed, the responsible party shall bear the corresponding liability.

(4) Technical Intermediary Contracts

82. The technical intermediary contract referred to in Article 364 of the Contract Law of the PRC refers to a contract concluded by one party using its knowledge, technology, experience, and information to contact and introduce the other party to a third party for the conclusion of a technology contract, to organize commercialization and industrialization development, and to provide services for the performance of the contract, excluding various brokerage contracts that do not contain technical intermediary service content.

83. The main obligations of the client under a technical intermediary contract are to put forward clear contracting requirements and provide relevant background materials; to bear the expenses incurred by the intermediary in conducting intermediary activities as agreed; and to pay remuneration as agreed.

The main obligations of the intermediary are to truthfully reflect the technical achievements, credit status, and performance capabilities of the client and the third party; to keep confidential the business secrets of the client and the third party; and to provide services for the conclusion and performance of the contract between the client and the third party as agreed.

84. If the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the burden of expenses for the intermediary's intermediary activities, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the expenses shall be borne by the intermediary itself. If the parties agree that the expenses shall be borne by the client but do not agree on the amount or calculation method of the expenses, the client shall pay the necessary expenses incurred by the intermediary in conducting the intermediary activities.

The expenses for the intermediary's intermediary activities referred to in the preceding paragraph refer to the expenses for communication, transportation, and necessary investigation and research incurred by the intermediary in conducting contact and introduction activities before the client and the third party conclude the technology contract.

85. If the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the amount of remuneration for the intermediary, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the remuneration shall be reasonably determined based on the intermediary's labor and shall be borne by the client. If only intermediary clauses are agreed upon in the technology contract concluded between the client and the third party, but the obligation to pay remuneration to the intermediary is not agreed or is not clearly agreed, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the client and the third party shall bear the remuneration equally.

The remuneration for the intermediary referred to in the preceding paragraph refers to the income that the intermediary should receive for facilitating the conclusion of the technology contract between the client and the third party and for providing services for the performance of the contract.

86. If the intermediary fails to facilitate the conclusion of a technology contract between the client and the third party, the intermediary is not entitled to demand remuneration but may demand that the client pay the necessary expenses incurred in conducting the intermediary activities.

87. If the intermediary intentionally conceals important facts related to the conclusion of the technology contract or provides false information, thereby harming the interests of the client, the intermediary shall bear the liability of waiving remuneration and compensating for damages.

88. The expenses for intermediary activities and remuneration collected by the intermediary shall not be regarded as losses of either party in a dispute over the technology contract between the client and the third party.

89. If the intermediary has no fault in causing the technology contract between the client and the third party to be invalid or rescinded, and the invalidity or rescission does not affect the continued validity of the relevant intermediary clauses or the technical intermediary contract, the intermediary is still entitled to collect the expenses for intermediary activities and remuneration as agreed.

V. Procedural Issues Related to Hearing Technology Contract Disputes

(1) Jurisdiction and Acceptance of Technology Contract Disputes

90. Technology contract disputes are disputes related to intellectual property rights and shall be under the jurisdiction of intermediate people's courts or above, except as otherwise determined by the Supreme People's Court.

91. If a contract contains both technology contract content and other contract content, and the parties have disputes over both the technology contract content and other contract content, the case shall be accepted by the people's court with jurisdiction over technology contract dispute cases.

92. If one party claims that the technology contract under dispute infringes upon the technological achievements of others and requests that the contract be invalidated, or if the people's court discovers during the hearing of a technology contract dispute that there may be such a ground for invalidity, it shall timely notify the interested party to participate in the proceedings as a third party with independent claims.

93. If another person brings a claim of ownership or infringement regarding the technology that is the subject matter of the technology contract to the people's court hearing the technology contract dispute, and the court receiving the case also has jurisdiction over that claim, it may hear the ownership or infringement dispute together with the contract dispute. If the court receiving the case does not have jurisdiction over that claim, it shall inform the claimant to file a separate lawsuit with the competent people's court. After the ownership or infringement dispute is accepted in a separate case, the contract dispute proceeding shall be suspended.

94. In a lawsuit concerning a patent implementation license contract, if the licensee (licensee) or a third party requests the Patent Reexamination Board to declare the patent right invalid, the people's court may not suspend the proceedings. If the patent right is declared invalid during the proceedings, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Patent Law of the PRC.

95. Disputes arising from the intermediary's breach of the agreed confidentiality obligation in a technical intermediary contract may be heard together with the technology contract dispute.

96. The intermediary shall generally not be a party to a lawsuit concerning the technology contract between the client and the third party, except in the following circumstances:

(1) If the intermediary maliciously colludes with one party to the technology contract to harm the interests of the other party, the maliciously colluding parties shall be listed as co-defendants and bear joint and several liability;

(2) If the intermediary conceals the true situation of one party to the technology contract and causes losses to the other party, the intermediary shall be listed as a defendant and bear corresponding liability according to its fault;

(3) If the intermediary fails to perform the technical intermediary contract or other obligations agreed in the intermediary clauses, resulting in the inability to perform the technology contract as agreed, the intermediary may be listed as a litigation party depending on the specific circumstances.

(2) Appraisal of the Technology Subject Matter of the Technology Contract

97. In a lawsuit over a technology contract dispute, if it is necessary to conduct an appraisal of the technology that is the subject matter of the contract, aside from the statutory appraisal departments, if the parties negotiate and recommend a mutually trusted organization or expert to conduct the appraisal, the people's court may designate such organization or expert. If the parties cannot reach an agreement, the people's court may select from and designate an appraisal organization or expert recommended by the provincial-level or higher science and technology administrative department, or may directly designate a relevant organization or expert to conduct the appraisal.

If an expert is designated to conduct the appraisal, an appraisal panel shall be formed. The number of appraisers shall be an odd number of three or more.

98. The appraisal shall take the technical achievements or technical service content agreed in the contract to be provided by the parties as the object of appraisal, and examine whether they can achieve the agreed technical indicators and economic benefit indicators from the aspects of principles, design, process, and necessary technical data, in accordance with the agreed testing methods and acceptance standards.

99. If the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the testing method or acceptance standard for the technical achievements, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the testing method or acceptance standard commonly used in the industry or practical may be adopted according to the specific circumstances of the case for testing and appraisal, expert review, or acceptance appraisal.

If the acceptance standard agreed in the contract is clear and the technical problem is not complicated, the technical achievements may be appraised by means of on-site demonstration, operation, or production by the parties.

100. If the parties to a technical consultation contract have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the method of acceptance or evaluation of the consultation report and opinions, and cannot reach a supplementary agreement in accordance with Article 61 of the Contract Law, the appraisal shall be conducted in accordance with general requirements for practicality.

101. For technical achievements that have already passed appraisal such as technical achievement appraisal or new product appraisal in accordance with relevant state regulations, and there is no contrary evidence sufficient to overturn the appraisal conclusion, or technical achievements that have been proven to be mature and reliable through actual use, if the parties subsequently dispute the evaluation of such technical achievements during the litigation, no further appraisal shall be conducted.

102. The relevant patent documents granting a patent right shall not be used as a substitute for the appraisal conclusion of the technology subject matter of the contract.
